title: Erythema multiforme: target lesions (herpes simplex-associated)
vignette: A 27-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of a new skin rash for the last day. She also has a history of recurrent genital lesions, which begin with small vesicles with subsequent ulceration, crusting, and eventual healing. The patient has no other medical conditions and takes no medications. On physical examination, she appears comfortable. Temperature is 37 C (98.6 F). She has small linear erosions in the oral mucosa. Skin findings show multiple erythematous, round papules that evolve into TARGET lesions - a dusky central area, a surrounding pale ring, and an outer erythematous halo - on the extremities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

clues.text: recurrent genital lesions, which begin with small vesicles with subsequent ulceration, crusting, and eventual healing
clues.note: Recurrent genital vesicles/ulcers describe herpes simplex virus (HSV) - the most common trigger of erythema multiforme.

clues.text: small linear erosions in the oral mucosa
clues.note: Mild mucosal (oral) involvement can occur in erythema multiforme (severe/major forms affect mucosa more).

clues.text: TARGET lesions - a dusky central area, a surrounding pale ring, and an outer erythematous halo
clues.note: TARGET (iris) lesions with a dusky center, pale ring, and erythematous halo are pathognomonic of erythema multiforme.

whatMatters: TARGET (iris) lesions - dusky center, pale ring, erythematous halo - on the extremities, in a patient with recurrent HSV, = ERYTHEMA MULTIFORME (EM). EM is a cell-mediated (CD8+) reaction most often triggered by HERPES SIMPLEX VIRUS (also Mycoplasma, drugs). Answer B.
strategy: Recognize the classic TARGET lesions of erythema multiforme and its strong HSV association. Reject the mimics: disseminated HSV (diffuse vesicles in immunocompromised, not target lesions), primary HIV (macular rash + fever, trunk/palms/soles), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (drug-induced, skin sloughing/systemic toxicity - more severe), and varicella (vesicles in different stages, not targets).

eliminations.label: Disseminated HSV - diffuse vesicles (immunocompromised)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: widespread HSV vesicles on an erythematous base in immunocompromised patients. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient has TARGET lesions (a systemic immune response to HSV), not disseminated vesicular infection, and she is immunocompetent. ✅ Correct if: diffuse vesicles in an immunocompromised host.

eliminations.label: Primary HIV - macular rash + fever, trunk/palms/soles
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: acute retroviral syndrome with fever and a maculopapular rash on trunk/face/palms/soles. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's a well-circumscribed macular rash, not target lesions. ✅ Correct if: mononucleosis-like illness with a truncal rash and high-risk exposure.

eliminations.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome - drug-induced, skin sloughing
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a severe mucocutaneous reaction (often to sulfonamides, allopurinol, anticonvulsants) with erythematous macules, epidermal necrosis/sloughing, and systemic signs (fever, hypotension). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient is comfortable, afebrile, without skin sloughing; her HSV-triggered target lesions fit EM. ✅ Correct if: drug-triggered rash with mucosal involvement + skin detachment/systemic toxicity.

eliminations.label: Varicella - vesicles in different stages
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: chickenpox with a pruritic vesicular rash in crops (lesions at different stages). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it lacks the characteristic target lesions of EM. ✅ Correct if: fever + vesicles in different stages of development.

reasoning: Target (iris) lesions with a dusky center, pale ring, and erythematous halo on the extremities
History of recurrent HSV (genital lesions) - the classic trigger
Target lesions + HSV association = erythema multiforme
mechanism: Erythema multiforme (EM) is an acute, cell-mediated hypersensitivity reaction of the skin (and sometimes oral mucosa) characterized by erythematous papules that evolve into TARGET (iris) LESIONS - a dusky/necrotic central zone, a surrounding pale edematous ring, and an outer erythematous halo - typically on the EXTREMITIES (including palms/soles). Histologically there is a cell-mediated process with a cytotoxic CD8+ T-lymphocyte infiltrate directed against antigens (often viral) deposited in the skin. EM is most commonly triggered by infections - especially HERPES SIMPLEX VIRUS (as in this patient with recurrent genital HSV) and Mycoplasma pneumoniae - and less often by drugs (e.g., sulfonamides), malignancy, or autoimmune disease. It is usually self-limited; recurrent HSV-associated EM may warrant antiviral suppression. It sits at the mild end of a spectrum distinct from the more severe, usually DRUG-induced Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis (extensive epidermal sloughing, mucosal involvement, systemic toxicity). The other options (disseminated HSV, primary HIV, varicella) have different morphologies and don't produce target lesions.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Derm > erythema multiforme: target (iris) lesions on extremities; cell-mediated (CD8+); triggers = HSV (most common), Mycoplasma, drugs; contrast Stevens-Johnson (drug-induced, sloughing/systemic).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Target lesions + recurrent HSV = erythema multiforme.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on target/iris lesion, erythema multiforme vs Stevens-Johnson, or HSV trigger? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Disseminated HSV (diffuse vesicles), primary HIV (macular rash), SJS (drug/sloughing), varicella (crops) - none has target lesions.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the skin photo: round lesions with a dusky center, a pale ring, and an outer erythematous halo (target/iris lesions). Anchor: 'target lesions + HSV = erythema multiforme.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: erythema multiforme = target lesions, HSV-associated (also Mycoplasma); milder than Stevens-Johnson (drug-induced).

keywords.front: Most common trigger of erythema multiforme

keywords.back: Dusky center + pale ring + erythematous halo

firstAid.detail: Derm > SJS (drug/sloughing), disseminated HSV, primary HIV, varicella.

memoryHook: Bull's-eye rings on the arms in someone with recurrent herpes = erythema multiforme - the immune system's 'target practice' against HSV antigens in the skin.
